turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you. I came in today because I'm having a really hard time turning my thoughts off. Once a worry starts, I just can't seem to put it away. It could be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or just worrying if I missed some detail at work. 

I try to redirect myself, and I make plenty of lists to stay organized, but I just can't seem to shelve those thoughts once they get going. It doesn't matter how hard I try, I just can't stop focusing on them.

symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient explicitly describes an inability to control or stop their worries despite active attempts to redirect themselves.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying and difficulty turning off your thoughts?
turns.patient_response: It's been about... a year and two months, I'd say. It started right around the time my mother moved into my home after she had a fall.

turns.doctor_question: Along with this constant worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, or being easily fatigued?
turns.patient_response: Yes, definitely the muscle tension. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders just feel completely locked up... it's like I'm constantly bracing myself for something. And I actually catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, too, especially while I'm answering emails or just, you know, listening for my mother in the next room.

symptom_reasoning.S061: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing muscle tension, describing locked-up neck and shoulders and frequent jaw clenching throughout the day.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying just as much even on days when your mother's care is going smoothly and there's no immediate crisis with her?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Even if she's having a good day and resting quietly, the worrying doesn't stop. Over this past year, it's just spread. At first it was just about her safety, but now it's about... well, everything. Finances, decisions I have to make about my staff at the library, deadlines for reports, keeping up with the house, and just constantly questioning if I'm being a good enough daughter. It feels like even the small things start to feel like they're about to completely unravel, no matter how calm the day is supposed to be.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms that her worrying does not stop and has spread to multiple different areas of life, including work, finances, and household responsibilities, even when situations are calm.

turns.doctor_question: Would you say you've been experiencing this level of worry and muscle tension on most days, more days than not, over the past several months?
turns.patient_response: Yes, definitely. I'd say... well, it's almost every day, to be honest. More days than not, for sure. I really can't remember the last time I went a full day without feeling that tension or having my mind racing about something.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms experiencing persistent worry occurring almost every day, more days than not, over the past several months.
symptom_reasoning.S061: The patient explicitly affirms having tension nearly every day, agreeing with the doctor's inquiry regarding frequent muscle tension.
